authorship: AI-assisted expectations independently derived from pinned rule bytes and saved Oracle text; model confidence and agreement between engines are not evidence.
observation_disclosure: The author derived and froze these projections without viewing any new spell-copy native, Forge or XMage outputs. The six scenario sequences and aliases were coordinated before projection authorship. Prior instant-interaction expectations were read for format only. Two independent source/implementation reviewers subsequently approved these fixed projections and native boundary groups; review metadata is a manual workflow record, not a formal proof.
scope: Six fixed-world, single-target Lightning Bolt copies made by Twincast; 38 common stable stack/card checkpoints. This is restricted resolution/target/counter/cleanup evidence, not complete casting, mana payment, priority scheduling, whole-card, full-game or performance qualification.

common_projection_contract.cards: Exactly the six seeded physical card aliases; a spell copy has no physical card and appears only as its own stack entry while on the stack.
common_projection_contract.target_aliases: Aliases identify the originally captured battlefield or stack object incarnation, including stale references. A matching alias in a new zone does not mean target recapture.
common_projection_contract.stable_boundary: Every common checkpoint follows applicable state-based actions. Copy graveyard entry and subsequent cessation are separately asserted only at native boundaries.
common_projection_contract.nonbattlefield_characteristics: Power, toughness and marked damage are intentionally null outside the battlefield in this projection; this does not assert that a creature card has no printed characteristics in other zones.

setup.unmodeled_effects: No prevention, replacement, regeneration, indestructibility, target restrictions, triggers or other effects change these vanilla interactions.

bolt.name: Lightning Bolt
bolt.text: Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target.

twincast.name: Twincast
twincast.text: Copy target instant or sorcery spell. You may choose new targets for the copy.

bounce.name: Unsummon
bounce.text: Return target creature to its owner's hand.

semantic_expectations.expectation: The created copy is an independent spell with no associated physical card, owned and controlled by B even though A owns and controls the original. It is not cast and does not initiate or pay a new casting cost.

Copy the Bolt characteristics, executable three-damage instruction and original target choice. Only the optional target change expressly allowed by Twincast is made anew here. Modes, X, divisions and additional/alternative-cost decisions are general rule obligations beyond the exercised Bolt payload; resolution-time choices are not copied.

An unchanged inherited target may already be illegal at copy creation. A changed target must be legal at copy creation. Never replace a stale target with the card's new incarnation or choose a default target.

Original and copy leave the stack independently. Resolution, countering and all-targets-illegal removal move this instant spell copy to its owner's graveyard. It remains present off-stack until a distinct state-based action makes it cease to exist.

negative_contract_expectations.input: Retain the inherited lion1 battlefield incarnation after Unsummon has returned lion1 to hand.
negative_contract_expectations.expected: Accept copy creation with that stale inherited target; later resolution fails its all-targets-illegal check.

negative_contract_expectations.input: Choose the lion1 card now in hand as a changed creature target, or supply the departed battlefield incarnation as a changed target.
negative_contract_expectations.expected: Reject the changed target atomically; do not create a copy, pay any copy casting cost, recapture the card or change the original.

negative_contract_expectations.input: Counter or resolve either original or copy while the other remains on the stack.
negative_contract_expectations.expected: The surviving spell retains its own stack identity, controller, executable payload and target choices.

cases.reasoning: Twincast resolves and B chooses the still-legal lion2 as the copy target. The new Bolt spell copy is owned and controlled by B; the original remains A's spell targeting lion1. The copy resolves first, marks three damage on lion2 and goes to B's graveyard as the final part of resolution. State-based actions destroy lion2 and make the off-stack copy cease to exist before the next common checkpoint. The original then resolves against lion1; its physical card and the lethally damaged lion1 finish in their owners' graveyards.

After B creates a copy targeting lion2, A's Counterspell targets only the original Bolt. Counterspell removes the original without any original Bolt effect, so lion1 remains undamaged. This does not remove or alter the already created independent copy. The copy resolves against lion2 and then ceases to exist at the subsequent state-based checks; lion2 is destroyed for lethal damage. The physical original Bolt and Counterspell are in A's graveyard, and Twincast is in B's graveyard.

Counterspell may target the copy because a copy of a spell is itself a spell. It removes only that copy without any copy effect. The copy goes to its owner B's graveyard and ceases to exist as a later state-based action. The original Bolt remains on the stack and resolves against lion1. Thus lion1 dies, lion2 stays on the battlefield with no damage, and the two physical A spells finish in A's graveyard.

Unsummon resolves above Twincast and returns lion1 to B's hand. Twincast still legally targets the Bolt spell on the stack. CR 707.10c permits B to leave the inherited lion1 target unchanged even though its battlefield incarnation is already gone. The copy is created rather than rejected, and it retains that old target incarnation rather than following lion1 into hand. On its resolution check the copy's only target is illegal, so it does not resolve, goes to B's graveyard, and later ceases to exist. The original also does not resolve against its illegal target. Neither Bolt damages either Lion.

decisions.copy_targets: change to legal lion2 battlefield incarnation

cases.reasoning: Unsummon removes lion1 before Twincast resolves, but Bolt itself remains a legal Twincast target. The copy may be created despite the original's now-illegal creature target. B uses the permission to change that target to the still-legal lion2. The copy resolves, kills lion2 through lethal-damage state-based actions, and ceases to exist after leaving the stack. The original retains the old lion1 incarnation and does not resolve. lion1 stays in B's hand; no target is silently captured again.

decisions.copy_targets: retain original legal lion1 battlefield incarnation
decisions.bounce_target: lion1 after the copy is created

cases.reasoning: B creates a copy retaining the currently legal lion1 target. A then resolves Unsummon above that copy, returning lion1 to B's hand. Both the copy and original retain the departed battlefield incarnation, so each has no legal target when checked in order. Neither resolves or deals damage. The copy first goes to B's graveyard and then ceases to exist under state-based actions; the physical original finishes in A's graveyard. lion2 remains undamaged on the battlefield.
